marked_text:
Sigrid Moller, mast rigger, writing from the harbour shed in Nuuk once the fog lifted off the crane. Job [[job]]NUK-3184[[/]] belongs to customer [[customer]]Qaqortoq Freight[[/]], whose coastal set went quiet just after midnight. I stayed on the iced rungs for [[hours]]8.5[[/]] hours, and the rate card clipped beside the job says [[rate]]63.20[[/]]. An old quote of 480.65 was stapled under the clip; that slip is from another winter and I would not honour it. We buttoned the work up on [[done]]14 May 2026[[/]]. Stamp: MODTAGET. The mate kept saying qujanaq while the winch squealed over the basin. Nobody clipped a purchase order to this copy. A tear split ru
ngs on the carbon, so the office sheet looks as if the ladder failed twice.

ask.instruction: Job code printed on the Nuuk docket

ask.instruction: Hours multiplied by the rate on the card

marked_text:
Rain hammered the tin roof in Palikir and the gutter was already overflowing onto the step. Renato Halbert, radio tech, opened job [[job]]PLK-5521[[/]] when the VHF stack hissed and the night operator refused the climb. I swapped the [[part]]coax jumper[[/]], then a seized [[part]]mast clamp[[/]], then the [[part]]desiccant pack[[/]] that had melted into grey paste. Time on the ladder came to [[hours]]6[[/]] hours at the card rate of [[rate]]48.15[[/]]. Their quote, still pinned in the folder, reads 310.40, and that figure was never meant for this mast. I closed the docket on [[closed]]3 June 2026[[/]]. Stamp: FILED. The clerk pencilled kalahngan along the margin. Carbon broke the word lad
der, so the duplicate starts in the middle of a syllable.

marked_text:
The ferry horn kept cutting across the yard while Lagi Tuala, linesman, sat in the Apia depot with a soaked envelope. Job [[job]]API-7742[[/]] had bled ink at the corner. I logged [[fault]]salt crust on the lug[[/]], a [[fault]]cracked gland[[/]], and a [[fault]]loose earth braid[[/]] that sparked once the load came back. The slip shows a gross of [[gross]]640.80[[/]] set against a credit of [[credit]]115.30[[/]], and I left the remainder off the page. The case was opened on [[opened]]8 April 2026[[/]] and shut again on [[closed]]27 April 2026[[/]]. Old docket API-6610 sits in the same drawer and belongs to another feeder. Stamp: LOGGED. The watchman said faafetai as he locked the gate. The sheet ripped through gl
and, so the word is split across the tear.

ask.instruction: Gross figure minus the credit note

marked_text:
Erita Ioane, beacon keeper, writing in the south shed on Tarawa after the lagoon finally went flat and the skiff could tie up. Job [[job]]TRW-4418[[/]] covers the outer light past the reef. I worked the tasks in this order: [[task]]reset the beacon timer[[/]], [[task]]scrape coral off the base[[/]], [[task]]reseat the solar plug[[/]], and [[task]]paint the tide mark[[/]]. That round was finished on [[done]]19 August 2026[[/]]. The permit square on the card is still empty. Stamp: SEEN. An older card marked TRW-2201 belongs to a different beacon and stayed in the tin. The boatman called ko rabwa as he pushed off the jetty. Carbon tore bea
con apart, so the office copy looks unfinished and salty.

marked_text:
Caleb Joseph, cable jointer, from the river pit in Roseau once the water had dropped below the joint and the mud could hold a boot. Job [[job]]ROS-7731[[/]] is the splice we had to cut open again. We first went into the pit on [[opened]]2 February 2026[[/]] and we packed the joint and left on [[closed]]20 February 2026[[/]]. I am not writing how long we were down there. The wet folder also holds old ticket DOM-5504, which is the bath road job and not this pit. Stamp: PIT-OK. A neighbour leaned on the fence and said mesi, then nothing else. The carbon split jo
int, so the duplicate reads like two scraps of the same word. The ministry book is still in Portsmouth.

marked_text:
Inez Castillo, stores clerk, in the Belmopan cage with the fluorescent tube buzzing and a moth trapped in the shade. Job [[job]]BMP-6309[[/]] covers the western run out past the river. I handed across [[item]]tie wire[[/]], [[item]]bitumen tape[[/]], and one [[item]]warning flag[[/]] still in its paper sleeve. The three lines on the charge strip read [[charge]]42.15[[/]], [[charge]]18.60[[/]] and [[charge]]27.40[[/]], and I did not add them anywhere on the page. Last month this cage rolled up 73.90, a different issue entirely. The book was signed on [[issued]]11 November 2026[[/]]. Stamp: ISSUED. The driver muttered ya esta, took the flag, and left the gate open. The sheet tore through warn
ing, so the last item sits in two pieces.
